About.Name: Falisha Hill
About.AboutText:
Hello, I am Falisha Hill. I am a mechanical engineering student with an interest in metal working and 3D digital designing. I am currently pursuing my undergraduate degree at Seattle Pacific University. I am interested in expanding my knowledge and experience in designing and building, as well as more technical skills such as coding and working with circuits.

I enjoy physical and creative challenges when it comes to engineering, and work well in a team and with individual assignments.

Experience.ExperienceText:
Most of my professional experience has come from my job in a small company called Jodi’s Interiors, where I have gained experience primarily in warehouse and manufacturing environments, although I have also worked on-site for installations and to communicate with customers.

While I have become comfortable handling power tools and working around busy environments through this job, I have always had an interest in machines and robotics. This interest led me to attempt for a mechanical engineering degree through SPU. Currently, I am working my way through both the job and the degree.
Experience.EducationText: I am currently in my fifth year at SPU studying to achieve a mechanical engineering bachelor’s degree. My first four years were spent as a full time student, and I have transitioned to a part time role for the foreseeable future in my education.
Experience.EmploymentText:
I am one of the few main manufacturers in this company, as well as an assistant for installations when necessary. I have learned and become proficient in the creation of draperies, top treatments, and cornice boards over the years I have worked under this employer. These processes include tasks such as accurately checking, measuring, and cutting fabrics to size, sewing hems, and setting hooks and grommets to finish.

From this job I have become comfortable handling power tools such as drills, hand and power saws, pneumatic nailers, and pneumatic staplers.

Installation sites range between completely empty buildings to active construction where me and other installers have to maneuver around different workers and active projects
Experience.SkillsText:
I have a SOLIDWORKS Associate certification, issued by Dassault Systemes on November 1st, 2026.

While earning this certification, I have learned how to read professional blueprints for parts and accurately recreate them in the software using the tools available to me, how to create and alter configurations using global variables and by hand, as well as how to create and edit assemblies using different parts and references.

Project1.Title: Renton Weatherly Inn
Project1.Desc:
The Weatherly Inn was a project that spanned across three years, where Jodi’s Interiors was tasked with manufacturing and installing draperies and cornice boards throughout the entirety of the 5-story retirement facility. The team for the project had a total of five workers, and most laborers had to multitask between the manufacturing and installations.

I was one of the multitasking laborers, although my role was primarily a manufacturer for the first two years of the project alongside two other employees. Every pair of draperies needed to be cut to a specific length, hemmed, steamed, fanfolded, and bagged carefully to avoid damage during transportation. My responsibility split between manufacturing and installing during the last year due to the upcoming deadline for the facility to have every residential window covered to gain their licensing from the state.

In total, we created and installed a total of 962 pairs of draperies, spread throughout each bedroom and common room within the building.
